Theophrastus, as quoted by Burnet (Early Greek Philosophy 3rd ed. §13), calls Anaximander 'a fellow-citizen and associate of Thales'; Diogenes Laertius 2.1 places him in the same city and tradition. 'Associate' is weaker than 'pupil', so lineage_type is claimed.

Diogenes Laertius 9.50 (Hicks): 'Protagoras studied under Democritus.' RECORDED AS DOUBTFUL AND WHY: the same author's chronology contradicts it. DL 9.56 puts Protagoras's floruit in the 84th Olympiad (444-441), while DL 9.34 makes Democritus forty years younger than Anaxagoras, whose birth DL 2.7 places in the 70th Olympiad (500-497) — so Democritus would have been about seventeen when Protagoras was at the height of his career. The link is kept because the claim is in the source and readers meet it elsewhere; reliability low says what to do with it.

Diogenes Laertius 2.13 (Hicks) has Pericles say to the assembly 'I am a pupil of Anaxagoras; do not then be carried away by slanders and put him to death.' Reported speech in a third-century compilation, hence claimed and medium.
Shiji 67 lists him among the disciples and dates him by his age difference from Confucius (少孔子四十六歲). The Analects gives him sayings of his own (1.4, 8.3-7).
Shiji 67: 卜商字子夏。少孔子四十四歲. The Analects has Confucius address him directly (3.8, 6.11).

Shiji 67 lists him among the disciples; the Analects has Confucius rebuke him by name for enriching the Ji family (11.17) and question him about his ambitions (11.26). The Zuozhuan, Ai 11, shows him in the Ji family's service, which is what the rebuke is about.
